Terms

Term                          Definition
Gold Equivalent (AuEq)      : Refers to the equivalent value, expressed in terms of gold,
                              of different metals contained in an ore deposit. It is
                              generally denoted by the symbol “AuEq”.
Flotation                   : A separation and beneficiation process in which certain
                              minerals with different surface properties are floated in an
                              aqueous slurry, while others are allowed to settle.
Concentrate                 : The product or products obtained by enriching the target
                              minerals separated from run-of-mine (ROM) ore through
                              mineral processing and beneficiation.
Lump Ore                    : Ore that is suitable for direct processing due to its high
                              metal or valuable mineral content. Such ores can generally
                              be sent for smelting or refining without requiring
                              beneficiation.
Polymetallic Ore Deposit    : A term used to describe ore deposits containing more than
                              one metal. Such deposits generally contain lead (Pb), zinc
                              (Zn), copper (Cu), silver (Ag), gold (Au), and sometimes
                              other precious or industrial metals.
Mining Royalty (Rödovans)     An amount that an individual or legal entity undertaking
                              mining operations agrees to pay to the original licence
                              holder for each tonne of mineral produced, where the
                              licence holder grants the right to operate a licensed mining
                              area to that individual or entity for a specified period under
                              a contractual arrangement.
Grade                       : The percentage of a valuable element contained in an ore
                              or in a product obtained through ore beneficiation or
                              processing. More specifically, it is the ratio of the weight
                              of a particular element or compound in an ore sample to
                              the total dry weight of that sample, expressed as a
                              percentage.
Run-of-Mine (ROM) Ore       : Raw ore extracted directly from a mine without
                              undergoing any processing.
Beneficiation               : The process of converting run-of-mine materials (such as
                              ore, coal or industrial minerals) into marketable or
                              industrially usable products through physical and
                              physicochemical methods without altering their chemical
                              composition. In other words, run-of-mine material is
                              subjected to crushing, separation and classification
                              processes to produce concentrate, intermediate products
                              (middlings) and tailings.

About the Report

This Activity Report (the “Report”) has been prepared in accordance with the Capital Markets
Board’s (the “CMB” or the “Board”) Communiqué on Principles of Financial Reporting in Capital
Markets (II-14.1), which entered into force upon its publication in the Official Gazette dated 13 June
2013 and numbered 28676. The Report provides information on the activities of CVK Maden
İşletmeleri Sanayi ve Ticaret Anonim Şirketi (“CVK Madencilik”, the “Company” or the “Parent
Company”) and its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as the “Group”) during the interim accounting
period from 1 January 2026 to 30 September 2026.


About Us

CVK Madencilik was established on 15 August 2006 under the name CVK Krom Maden Sanayi ve
Ticaret A.Ş. to operate in the chrome mining sector. As the Company subsequently expanded its
operations into other metallic minerals, its corporate name was changed to CVK Maden İşletmeleri
Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş. on 16 November 2011.

The ÇEVİK family, which founded the Company, has a mining history spanning more than 40 years.
The founding family members obtained their first mining licence in 1980 and made their first
investment in mineral processing facilities in 1990 by establishing a Chrome Beneficiation Plant in
the Pınarbaşı district of Kayseri. They subsequently expanded their mining operations and, following
the establishment of CVK Madencilik, contributed to the Company's growth, helping it become one
of the leading companies in the sector.

CVK Madencilik made its first major investment in mineral processing facilities in 2012–2013 by
establishing a Lead and Zinc Flotation Plant in the Yenice district of Çanakkale. With a daily feed
capacity of 1,000 metric tonnes, the plant is capable of producing 30,000 metric tonnes of lead, zinc,
copper and silver concentrates annually.

In 2020, the Company made another significant investment by acquiring a majority stake in Hayri
Ögelman Madencilik A.Ş., one of Türkiye's first private-sector mining enterprises and a prominent
company in the chrome mining industry, thereby making it a subsidiary. Following the acquisition,
the Chrome Beneficiation Plant located in the Harmancık district of Bursa was modernised,
increasing its daily feed capacity to 1,000 metric tonnes and its annual chrome concentrate production
capacity to 36,000 metric tonnes. Furthermore, investments made in recent years have enabled the
mines within the licensed area where the plant is located to produce 12,000 metric tonnes per month
of high-grade, high-quality commercial lump chrome ore with a high chrome-to-iron ratio, suitable
for direct export.

In 2021, a majority stake in the Company was acquired by its current controlling shareholder, Hüseyin
ÇEVİK. In line with its long-term investment plans and growth objectives, the Company offered 20%
of its shares to the public in April 2023 and commenced trading on Borsa İstanbul. The Company
allocated 70% of the proceeds from its initial public offering to the Sarıalan Gold Mining Project in
the Altıeylül district of Balıkesir.

In 2024, the Company made significant investments by acquiring 100% of the shares of Orta Truva
Madencilik San. Tic. A.Ş. in Türkiye and 70% of the shares of Virtus Mining Ltd. abroad. Orta Truva
Madencilik San. Tic. A.Ş., a company established in Türkiye, is known in the mining sector for its
TV Tower Project located in Çanakkale. Virtus Mining Ltd., which is a tax resident of the
Netherlands, holds 100% of the shares of Aldridge Mineral Madencilik A.Ş., a company established
in Türkiye and known in the mining sector for its Yenipazar Project located in Yozgat. Consequently,
through these acquisitions, CVK Madencilik assumed control and management of both companies.

In 2025, having substantially completed its investments in the production plant and tailings storage
facility for the Sarıalan Gold Mining Project, the Company undertook initiatives to expand its licensed
mining area and acquired the adjacent Group IV mining area located within the boundaries of the
İvrindi district of Balıkesir, operating under Mining Operation Licence Registration No. 201201393.
In addition, in June 2025, the Company participated in a tender organised by the General Directorate
of Eti Maden Enterprises (Eti Maden) for the exploration and operation, in return for a royalty, of the
Kepsut gold locality situated within the Group IV licensed mining area bearing Registration No. 6406
in Balıkesir, held by Eti Maden. The Company won the tender by offering the highest royalty rate of
55.6%.

With the commencement of concentrate production at the Sarıalan Gold Mining Project in 2026, CVK
Madencilik aims to extend its strong position in chrome mining into gold mining, thereby further
strengthening its presence in the mining sector.

The Group is engaged in the production of lump and concentrate chrome ore, as well as gold, silver,
copper, lead and zinc concentrates, from its licensed mining areas, exporting a significant proportion
of its production. It also continuously carries out exploration and assessment activities in its other
licensed areas with high business development potential.

Established entirely with domestic capital, the Company conducts its operations through its mining
facilities and specialised personnel, with the objective of making the most effective use of Türkiye's
underground mineral resources and in accordance with its environmentally responsible approach to
sustainable mining. By employing modern engineering practices and leveraging technological
advancements, the Company continues to expand the impact and scale of its operations. It produces
high-quality chrome, lead, zinc and magnesite ores while continuing its investments in gold ore
production.

Operating mining facilities in various provinces across Türkiye, the Company attaches importance
and gives priority to providing environmentally responsible, safe and secure working environments
that comply with national and international standards at all its operations.

CVK Madencilik has adopted a sustainable mining approach that prioritises modern engineering
practices, employee health and occupational safety, while maintaining responsibility towards the
environment, society and applicable laws, with the objective of making the most effective use of
Türkiye's underground mineral resources. Accordingly, the Company undertakes initiatives to
develop sustainable mining practices, minimise environmental impacts, reduce water and energy
consumption, ensure sustainable raw material procurement, manage waste and rehabilitate mining
sites.

Mining Operations

       Harmancık Chrome Operation

Harmancık Chrome Operation, one of Türkiye's first private-sector mining enterprises, was
established in 1955 under the name Hayri Ögelman Ltd. Şti. It was renamed Hayri Ögelman
Madencilik Ltd. Şti. in 1959 and, following a change in its legal form in 2012, adopted its current
name, Hayri Ögelman Madencilik A.Ş. In 2020, CVK Madencilik acquired 86.21% of the shares in
Hayri Ögelman Madencilik A.Ş., followed by a further 10% in 2022, making it a 96.21%-owned
subsidiary.

Hayri Ögelman Madencilik A.Ş., which has operated in chrome mining since its establishment in
1955, holds a total of 10 mining areas with operation licences, most of which are located in the Bursa
region.

Hayri Ögelman Madencilik A.Ş.'s Harmancık Chrome Operation is located approximately 6.5 km
northwest of Harmancık district in Bursa province. The 6,306.87-hectare licensed operation area
contains underground and open-pit mines, administrative buildings and a chrome beneficiation
(concentrate) plant. High-grade lump chrome ore, which accounts for a substantial portion of the run-
of-mine ore produced in the underground and open-pit mines, can be exported directly without
undergoing any processing. Low-grade chrome ore is processed at the chrome beneficiation plant to
increase its grade and produce chrome concentrate, a significant portion of which is exported.

Following the inclusion of Harmancık Chrome Operation in the Group, capacity expansion activities
were initiated for the underground mines and chrome beneficiation plant in the region. Through the
investments made, run-of-mine ore production was increased under the project to connect the
underground mines in the region through tunnels. Machinery and equipment were also renewed as
part of the major maintenance and refurbishment project at the chrome beneficiation plant, bringing
its daily feed capacity to 1,000 metric tonnes. Following these investments, the underground mines
in the region can produce 12,000 metric tonnes of directly marketable lump chrome ore per month,
while the refurbished chrome beneficiation plant can produce 3,000 metric tonnes of chrome
concentrate per month.

However, the plant operates intermittently because the existing production areas in the region do not
produce sufficient quantities of low-grade chrome ore to continuously feed the chrome beneficiation
plant. During periods when the plant is shut down, the small quantities of low-grade chrome ore
produced at the mines are stockpiled in the plant's feed area, and the plant resumes operations once
sufficient feed material has accumulated. New production areas have been planned to increase low-
grade chrome ore production, and permit applications have been submitted. With the new
investments, the aim is to operate the chrome beneficiation plant continuously and further increase
production volumes.

      Kalkım Lead-Zinc Operation

CVK Madencilik's Kalkım Lead-Zinc Operation is located approximately 3.5 km southeast of Kalkım
town in Yenice district of Çanakkale province. The 1,609.14-hectare licensed operation area contains
underground mines, administrative buildings, a flotation plant and a tailings storage facility. Run-of-
mine ore produced from the underground mines is processed at the flotation plant into lead and zinc
concentrates, a significant portion of which is exported.

Following the completion of exploration activities in the licensed area in the Kalkım region in 2012,
preparations for run-of-mine ore production commenced. A fully automated flotation plant with a
daily feed capacity of 1,000 metric tonnes was installed in 2012–2013 to process the run-of-mine ore,
and a tailings storage facility was constructed.

The fully mechanised underground mines in the licensed area in the Kalkım region have an annual
run-of-mine ore production capacity of 500,000 metric tonnes. The flotation plant, with an annual
feed capacity of 300,000 metric tonnes, can produce 30,000 metric tonnes of lead, zinc, copper and
silver concentrates annually from the processed run-of-mine ore.

To support the production of run-of-mine ore required to feed the flotation plant in the Kalkım region,
capacity expansion activities were undertaken. Accordingly, new lead-zinc mining areas with
operation licences were acquired in the Çanakkale-Yenice and İzmir-Bayındır regions in 2017, while
a new lead-zinc mining area with an exploration licence was acquired through a MAPEG tender in
the Balıkesir-İvrindi region in 2019.

Run-of-mine ore production activities were suspended in 2022 because the existing tailings storage
facility of the flotation plant in the Kalkım region had reached its capacity. An Environmental Impact
Assessment (“EIA”) application has been submitted for the construction of an additional tailings
storage facility. If a positive EIA decision is obtained, construction of the tailings storage facility is
planned to commence and be completed.

village in Bayındır district of İzmir province. The 941.20-hectare licensed operation area contains
underground mines and administrative buildings. Following the acquisition of the area in 2017,
drilling and reserve determination activities were completed, statutory obligations were fulfilled, and
run-of-mine ore production commenced in 2019. Run-of-mine ore produced from the underground
mines is transported to the flotation plant in the Çanakkale-Yenice-Kalkım region, where it is
processed into lead and zinc concentrates, a significant portion of which is exported. Run-of-mine ore
production activities were suspended in 2022 because the existing tailings storage facility of the
flotation plant in the Kalkım region had reached its capacity. The “Agreement on the Transfer of

The Group IV mining area with Operation Licence No. S.72474, located near Yenipazar town in the

sustainable mining investment. Following Aldridge’s acquisition of the Yenipazar Project in 2006,
extensive exploration and drilling activities were carried out in certain parts of the licensed area,
revealing its mineral potential in detail and providing important technical data for the development
of the project. As a result of these activities, a Positive Environmental Impact Assessment (“EIA”)
Decision was obtained in 2014 for the Polymetallic Mining Operation and Ore Beneficiation Plant
covering 966.29 hectares of the licensed area, successfully completing one of the most significant

Business Model

The Group, which operates in the production of chrome, lead and zinc ores, holds a significant
position in the mining industry. With the Sarıalan Project, the Group will also commence gold
concentrate production.

Pursuant to Article 101/1 of the Mining Regulation, the Group has entered into mining royalty
agreements with third parties for the purpose of conducting mining activities in certain licensed areas
belonging to the Group.

Mining operation licence holders are required to notify the General Directorate of Mining and
Petroleum Affairs (“MAPEG”) of mining royalty agreements concluded with third parties concerning
all or part of their licensed areas, as well as any amendments to such agreements, and to have these
agreements annotated in the mining registry for information purposes. MAPEG is not a party to
mining royalty agreements under any circumstances. Mining royalty agreements are annotated in the
registry records as of the date on which MAPEG grants its approval.

The Group is entitled, at any time, to inspect the activities of the mining royalty contractor at the site,
its commercial and operational accounting records, production maps and production activities
through on-site measurements, ore shipments, records at the delivery location, and any other relevant
documents arising from the agreement, as well as to request copies and conduct audits. All
administrative, financial and legal responsibilities relating to labour law, occupational health and
occupational safety arising from mining royalty activities carried out under the agreement rest with
the mining royalty contractor.

Due to the nature of its activities, the Group is subject to the provisions of the Mining Law and the
Mining Regulation concerning the extension of mining licence periods. Accordingly, the Group
submits applications to MAPEG for the extension of its existing licences, together with the required
information and documentation, no later than twelve months before the expiry date of the relevant
licence. MAPEG must issue a favourable decision following its inspection.

Dividend Distribution Policy

The Company's Dividend Distribution Policy is as follows:

   Purpose

The purpose of the Dividend Distribution Policy is to establish the Company's dividend distribution
principles in accordance with the regulations to which the Company is subject and the provisions of
its Articles of Association, and to enable shareholders to anticipate the procedures and principles
governing the distribution of profits that the Company may generate in future periods. The Company
exercises the utmost care to maintain a balance between the interests of its shareholders and those of
the Company in matters relating to dividend distribution.

With regard to dividend distribution, the Company complies with Capital Markets Law No. 6362
(“CML”), Turkish Commercial Code No. 6102 (“TCC”), capital markets legislation, and other
applicable laws and regulations. The Company exercises the utmost care to comply with the
Corporate Governance Principles set out in the Corporate Governance Communiqué of the Capital
Markets Board (“CMB”).

The Company's Dividend Distribution Policy has been prepared in accordance with the CMB's
Corporate Governance Communiqué (II-17.1) and Dividend Communiqué (II-19.1) and is disclosed
to all stakeholders, particularly shareholders, through the Public Disclosure Platform (“PDP”) and the
Company's website (www.cvkmadencilik.com.tr).

   Authority and Responsibility

The Dividend Distribution Policy has been established by the Board of Directors within the
framework of the CMB Corporate Governance Principles and will be submitted for shareholder
approval as a separate agenda item at the Company's first General Assembly Meeting. The Board of
Directors is responsible for monitoring, overseeing, developing and making any necessary updates to
the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy. Following a resolution of the Board of Directors,
amendments to the Dividend Distribution Policy are publicly disclosed together with their
justifications in accordance with the regulations governing the disclosure of material events, approved
by the General Assembly and published on the Company's website (www.cvkmadencilik.com.tr).

   Dividend Distribution Principles

As a general principle, provided that the applicable regulations and financial resources permit,
decisions regarding dividend distribution are made by taking into account market expectations, our
long-term strategy, the capital requirements of the Company and its subsidiaries, investment and
financing policies, profitability and cash position. Dividends may be distributed to shareholders in
cash or in the form of bonus shares through the capitalisation of profits, or partly in cash and partly
in bonus shares at specified proportions.

Dividends are distributed equally to all existing shares as of the distribution date, in proportion to
their shareholdings, regardless of their issuance or acquisition dates. The Company does not have any
shares carrying dividend privileges.

Unless the legal reserves required under the TCC and the dividends designated for shareholders in
the Articles of Association or the Dividend Distribution Policy have been allocated, no decision may
be made to allocate other reserves, carry profits forward to the following year, or distribute shares of
profits to members of the Board of Directors, Company employees or persons other than shareholders.

Sustainability

CVK Madencilik adopts a sustainable mining approach that prioritises modern engineering practices,
employee health and occupational safety, and responsibility towards the environment, society and the
law, with the aim of making the best possible use of Türkiye's underground resources. In this regard,
the Company carries out activities to develop sustainable mining practices, minimise environmental
impacts, reduce water and energy consumption, ensure sustainable raw material sourcing, manage
waste and rehabilitate mining sites.

In a world where water resources are limited, the sustainable use of water is becoming increasingly
important. Adopting a life-cycle approach, CVK Madencilik takes care to minimise its direct and
indirect environmental impacts related to water through monitoring, measurement and efficiency
improvement activities at various stages of its operations.

The protection and management of biodiversity constitute an important part of CVK Madencilik's
environmental protection activities. The Company's fundamental approach in this area is based on
ensuring that the impacts of its operations on biodiversity are assessed, monitored and reported.

Having decided to invest in renewable energy sources to meet the energy requirements of its mining
sites and reduce energy costs, CVK Madencilik, as a Group, carries out activities relating to renewable
energy, particularly the installation of solar power plants. In this context, the Company's subsidiary,
Hayri Ögelman Madencilik A.Ş., completed the installation of a ground-mounted Solar Power Plant
(“SPP”) with a DC capacity of 2.473 MWp in Sivas province, which commenced electricity

Occupational Health and Safety

CVK Madencilik aims to conduct its operations in a healthy and safe working environment and to
provide suitable working conditions that contribute to building a sustainable future.

CVK Madencilik continues its occupational health and safety journey with the objective of “Zero
Occupational Accidents and Occupational Diseases.” The Group's occupational health and safety
practices reflect the value and importance it places on people and employees. Business continuity is
ensured through the confidence gained from strategies that adapt to the requirements of the times.

CVK Madencilik believes that providing employees with a healthy and safe working environment is
one of its fundamental priorities. While establishing safer working environments for employees
through preventive and corrective practices, the Company also protects employee health through
various projects and initiatives. In this context, the Company aspires to achieve excellence in the
implementation of occupational health and safety standards.

Providing a suitable working environment in which employees, subcontractors and relevant
stakeholders can carry out their activities under healthy and safe conditions, thereby contributing to
a sustainable future, is a priority for the Group. In line with this priority, CVK Madencilik eliminates
potential hazards and risks through proactive and systematic approaches.

Occupational health and safety activities are closely monitored by teams comprising occupational
safety specialists, occupational physicians and other healthcare personnel working within CVK
Madencilik, and necessary improvements are implemented. Occupational health and safety activities
are carried out under the leadership of the Occupational Health and Safety Units/professionals within
the Group, in coordination with the relevant departments.

CVK Madencilik, which undertakes significant responsibilities in putting its commitment to
occupational health and safety into practice, manages the regular review of practices at its operations,
the sharing and adoption of international developments and examples of good practice among Group
companies, and regulatory compliance processes through its Occupational Health and Safety Unit.

In addition to basic occupational health and safety training organised to increase employee awareness,
employees are provided with the necessary training and regular information. CVK Madencilik's
emergency action plans, prepared by taking into account potential emergencies at its operations, are
updated in accordance with statutory periods and requirements. Teams established under the
emergency action plans (firefighting, rescue, protection, first aid, etc.) receive training from
institutions and individuals authorised under the relevant legislation, and drills are conducted at least
once a year in accordance with predetermined scenarios.

Occupational health and safety risks are discussed by the Early Detection of Risk Committees of
CVK Madencilik's Group companies, and action implementation and monitoring processes are
carried out following committee meetings. These activities are also audited in terms of compliance
and internal control requirements within the framework of annual audit work plans. The Group's
governing bodies are regularly informed about the occupational health and safety activities of Group
companies.
